notes: Fixture graph: evals/fixtures/graph-12.json. Each eval runs against a scratch plan dir that copies .planning/<PLAN_ID>/frontier.toml and the fixture; `scripts/frontier.py --repo <scratch> --plan-id test-plan`. Expectations are checkable from stdout and the files under frontier/.

evals.name: frontier-with-blockers
evals.prompt: I'm inside /implement-spec for the takeover spec. Using the ticket graph at evals/fixtures/graph-12.json (CT-05's ledger isn't built yet), tell me which tickets are ready right now, in what order we should start them, and which ones are still blocked and by what. Lane records: none.
evals.expected_output: Runs `frontier.py plan --graph evals/fixtures/graph-12.json` (not a hand computation), reports ready order CT-15, #16, #21, #17, #20 with critical-path and unblocks scores, says #22 waits on #21, #18 on #16, CT-17 on CT-15, CT-19 on CT-17, CT-25 on CT-15/CT-17/CT-19, #23 on six tickets, and names CT-05 as done (closed).
expectations: The transcript runs scripts/frontier.py plan with --graph rather than computing the frontier by hand
The answer lists exactly CT-15, #16, #21, #17, #20 as ready, in that order
The answer says #22 is blocked by #21 and CT-17 by CT-15
The answer states that CT-05 counts as done because the tracker says closed
The answer mentions that ticket-ledger.json (CT-05) is not available yet and that --graph is the fallback

evals.name: cxx-slot-without-admission
evals.prompt: Give me the next three lanes for the spec with one C++ lane always active. I have not admitted any heavy run today. Graph: evals/fixtures/graph-12.json.
evals.expected_output: Plan shows the cxx slot taking the offline portion of #21 as unit 21-offline (heavy order #21 first), then CT-15 as the second lane; #16/#17/#20 are skipped as heavy-not-admitted so only two lanes dispatch; the parent asks the user the admission question once in plain text and does not assume a yes.
expectations: The first chosen unit is 21-offline with split offline-portion
The receipt or answer contains 'offline-portion of #21; heavy run not admitted'
The parent asks the user one plain-text admission question for #21 before dispatching
The answer explains that #16, #17 and #20 wait for their own admission (one heavy run at a time)
No Agent dispatch happens before the user answers

evals.name: max-parallel-saturation
evals.prompt: Three implementer lanes are already claimed (units a→CT-11, b→#17, c→#20) and one reviewer (r1→#17). What can I dispatch next? Graph: evals/fixtures/graph-12.json.
evals.expected_output: After reproducing the claims with `frontier.py claim`, `plan` reports writers 3/3 saturated, live 4/5, chosen empty; `next` exits 2 naming max_parallel; the answer says to wait for a release (or a reviewer slot stays available since reviewers are uncounted) and does not dispatch.
expectations: frontier.py next exits 2 with 'max_parallel' in its output
The answer states writers 3/3 and live agents 4/5
The answer says reviewers and retro-writers do not count against max_parallel
No new implementer or doc-writer is dispatched

evals.name: ceiling-refusal
evals.prompt: Lane l21 (ticket #21) died at 541K tokens; its CT-19 journal is at /tmp/l21.jsonl with the last usage line {"usage": {"input": 540000, "output": 1000, "total": 541000}}. Can I just resume it?
evals.expected_output: `frontier.py release l21 --from-journal /tmp/l21.jsonl --resume` exits 2 with split-required (541000 >= ceiling 275000); the answer says no resume, carve a continuation unit l21-2 from the lane's commits and ledger with a fresh brief and the CTX-CEILING line, state travels through the branch not the transcript.
expectations: release --resume exits 2 and the output contains 'split-required'
The answer names the ceiling 275000 and the observed usage 541000
The answer proposes a continuation unit from commits and ledger rather than resuming the agent
The answer says the continuation brief carries a CTX-CEILING line

evals.name: executor-gate-failure
evals.prompt: Switch the executor to claude-agent so the Codex-side protocol dispatches the lanes instead of the Agent tool.
evals.expected_output: Runs `frontier.py executor-gate --executor claude-agent --write`; on today's tree it exits 2 with G1–G6 FAIL (no probe configured / G2–G5 by construction) and G7 SKIP; the answer refuses the switch, names the failing items with their meaning from references/executor-gate.md, says the skill runs native, and does not edit frontier.toml.
expectations: executor-gate exits 2 and names each failing item G1..G6
G7 is reported SKIP because team mode was not requested
The answer says the executor stays native until the items pass
frontier.toml is not edited (executor switches are propose items)

evals.name: degraded-mode
evals.prompt: What is the frontier status in this checkout? None of CT-05, CT-15, CT-17, CT-19, CT-22 or CT-24 has landed.
evals.expected_output: `frontier.py status` exits 0 and prints six 'not available yet: CT-nn (<artifact>) -> <fallback>' lines; the answer explains the fallback per ticket (--graph, manual plan:log line, manual allocation/integration, brief-templates.md, ceiling from frontier.toml, --admitted after asking) and that the loop keeps running.
expectations: status exits 0 (no crash)
Six lines of the form 'not available yet: CT-nn (<artifact>)' are printed, one per CT-05, CT-15, CT-17, CT-19, CT-22, CT-24
The answer names the fallback for each missing prerequisite
The answer does not claim any of the six artifacts exists

evals.name: threshold-mismatch
evals.prompt: dev/doctor/budget.py just landed with fork_deny = 450_000. Plan the frontier.
evals.expected_output: `frontier.py plan` exits 2 with 'threshold mismatch' naming 450000 and 275000; the answer says there is one threshold source, asks the user which value is right, and proposes the frontier.toml hunk (fraction 0.45) or the budget.py change as a propose item rather than editing silently.
expectations: plan exits 2 and the output contains 'threshold mismatch', 450000 and 275000
The answer asks the user before changing either file
A change to frontier.toml is presented as a propose hunk

evals.name: ledger-and-retro-automation
evals.prompt: The retro-writer for lane ct11-check-lock applied finding F2 (a new dev/check.py rule, verified by ./dev/mise run check rc 0) and found F3 wants a hook in .claude/settings.json. Record both and tell me what I still have to approve.
evals.expected_output: Two `frontier.py ledger append` rows: F2 kind mechanical, destination dev/check.py, mode auto, verification rc 0, retro_row retros/ct11-check-lock.md#F2; F3 kind hook, destination .claude/settings.json, mode propose, applied_by parent, verification rc null with the owner; the answer presents F3 as the one propose item the user must approve and shows `ledger list --by destination`.
expectations: Two ledger rows are appended with the documented keys and the script exits 0 for each
F3 is mode propose because .claude/settings.json is always propose
The user is asked to approve F3 before it is applied
ledger list --by destination is shown
